### Observed differences

- The routing around A03 changed completely. In the earlier window, A02 and A04 led mostly to A03 (about 91% and 67% of their observed outgoing transitions), and A03 led mostly to A12 and A11 (about 45% each). In the later window, A02 and A04 lead only to A12, while A03 leads to A11 (about 55%) and A10 (about 45%). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- A16 changed successor: before, its outgoing transitions went to A10 (about 52%) and A09 (about 48%); in the later window they go to A09 (about 50%) and A03 (about 50%). [DIR004]
- A03's execution partners changed. Before, A03 and A12 always appeared together (co-occurring in about 49 in 100 traces, never one without the other), and A03 never co-occurred with A10 or A16. In the later window, A03 and A12 never co-occur (A03 without A12 in about 30 in 100 traces, A12 without A03 in about 45), while A03 co-occurs with A16 and with A10 in about 30 in 100 traces each, in varying order (mostly interleaved, A16 before A03 in about 7 in 100, A03 before A10 in about 13 in 100). A03 also stopped co-occurring with A02 and A04 (from about 25 and 24 in 100 traces to never). [REL004, REL003, REL005, REL001, REL002]
- Distances changed accordingly. A12 now immediately follows A02 and A04 in every observed pair (a one-step gap in 100% of cases, versus gaps of two to four steps before). A10 no longer follows A16 immediately: observed gaps are now two or more steps (about 45% at two steps), whereas before about 85% of pairs were one step apart. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- Participation and placement shifted: A03 appears in about 30 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 49 before, and later within the trace (mean relative position about 0.67 versus 0.44). A12 appears slightly less often (about 45 versus 49 in 100) and much earlier in some traces (mean position about 0.71 versus 0.97, with about a quarter of its occurrences now at the very start). A16 and A10 keep similar participation (about 27–30 in 100 traces) with only small position shifts. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence directly supports a re-routing of control flow around A03: A03 moved from the branch where A02 and A04 fed into it and it fed into A12, to the branch where A16 feeds into it and it feeds into A10 (A11 remaining a successor in both windows). In the earlier window the chain ran A02/A04 → A03 → A12 with A12 at the end of the trace; in the later window A02 and A04 lead directly and immediately to A12, while A03 sits on the A16 branch between A16 and A10. This is shown by the successor changes of A02, A03, A04 and A16, by A03's co-occurrence partners flipping from A12/A02/A04 to A16/A10, and by the distance changes (A12 now adjacent to A02/A04; A10 now two or more steps after A16). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, POS001, POS003]

The volume of qualified evidence rules out chance as an explanation: 16 control-flow items qualified where about 0.21 would be expected if nothing had changed, and the items describe one coherent restructuring rather than scattered differences. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a single relocation of A03 from two separate rewirings (its removal from the A02/A04 branch plus insertion into the A16 branch), and the "only to A12" pattern for A02 and A04 rests on moderate supports (28 and 35 observed outgoing transitions in the later window), so rare alternative successors could go unobserved. The placement statements concern event order within traces, not clock time. [DIR001, DIR003, POS003]
